summary: Independent CPU request-path review reproduced the original preferred-sampling-params loss on the prepared base and verified that the exact candidate preserves explicit chat values while allowing omitted values to use server preferences. The candidate also fixes the previously reported required-tool and cross-kind output-constraint precedence failures.

tests.what_was_measured: Independent reproduction of the original unset-field preference loss and the explicit text/cross-kind constraint failures. The base produced OpenAI defaults instead of all non-coincident preferences and SamplingParams.verify rejected cross-kind merged constraints.

The same independent probe showed preferred values winning for omitted fields, the derived required-tool regex winning over a preferred regex, explicit text clearing preferred constraints, and regex/EBNF/JSON-schema cross-kind cases passing SamplingParams.verify.
Candidate regression suite: 8 tests passed with 3 subtests, covering preferences, explicit values, generation config fallback, constraints, and legacy native-request precedence.
Related protocol and serving-chat regressions: 178 tests passed with 93 subtests.
Patch whitespace integrity and Python compilation of every changed runtime source file.

gpu_execution.evidence: The original issue and candidate changes are confined to CPU request conversion and tokenizer-manager dictionary precedence; no model execution is needed to validate this contract.

remaining_limitations: No GPU/server/model-weight run was performed; this review does not claim model architecture, semantic generation, transport, or distributed-workload coverage.
No native source changed in the candidate, and repository-environment.json declares native as null, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The prepared environment emitted an existing NUMA-balancing warning and loaded AIter from /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-b1e5b939386b/cache/aiter/module_aiter_core.so; neither affected the CPU assertions.
The pytest environment reported an unknown asyncio_mode configuration warning; all selected tests still completed successfully.
